text:
The entropy change associated with the conversion of 1 kg of ice at 273 K to water vapours at 383 K is : 

(Specific heat of water liquid and water vapour are $4.2 kJ K^{-1} kg^{-1}$ and $2.0 kJ K^{-1} kg^{-1}$; heat of liquid fusion and vapourisation of water are $334 kJ kg^{-1}$ and $2491 kJ kg^{-1}$, respectively). (log 273 = 2.436, log 373 = 2.572, log 383 = 2.583)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The change is carried out in four steps, each for 1 kg.

Melting of ice at 273 K: $\Delta S_{1}=\dfrac{\Delta _{fus}H}{T}=\dfrac{334}{273}=1.223\text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$

Heating water from 273 K to 373 K: $\Delta S_{2}=c\ln \dfrac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=4.2\times 2.303\times (2.572-2.436)=1.315\text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$

Vaporisation at 373 K: $\Delta S_{3}=\dfrac{\Delta _{vap}H}{T}=\dfrac{2491}{373}=6.678\text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$

Heating vapour from 373 K to 383 K: $\Delta S_{4}=2.0\times 2.303\times (2.583-2.572)=0.051\text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$

$\Delta S_{\text{total}}=1.223+1.315+6.678+0.051=9.267\text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$

This is 9.26 $\text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$ within the rounding of the given logarithms; the other options are far from it.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text: For the reaction, 2A + B $\to$ products, when the concentrations of A and B both were doubled, the rate of the reaction increased from 0.3 mol $L^{-1}s^{-1}$ to 2.4 mol $L^{-1}s^{-1}$. When the concentration of A alone is doubled, the rate increased from 0.3 mol $L^{-1}s^{-1}$ to 0.6 mol $L^{-1}s^{-1}$.
options: Total order of the reaction is 4
Order of the reaction with respect to B is 2
Order of the reaction with respect to B is 1
Order of the reaction with respect to A is 2
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the reaction, write the rate law as

$r=k[\mathrm{A}]^{m}[\mathrm{B}]^{n}$

where $m$ and $n$ are the orders with respect to $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$.

When only $[\mathrm{A}]$ is doubled:

$\frac{0.6}{0.3}=2^{m}$

$2=2^{m}\Rightarrow m=1$

When both concentrations are doubled:

$\frac{2.4}{0.3}=2^{m+n}$

$8=2^{m+n}$

Since $8=2^{3}$,

$m+n=3$

Using $m=1$:

$1+n=3\Rightarrow n=2$

Thus, the order with respect to $\mathrm{B}$ is $2$.

$\text{Option B}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

solution.body:

text:
Which of the following combination of statements is true regarding the interpretation of the atomic orbitals ? 

(a) An electron in an orbital of high angular momentum stays away from the nucleus than an electron in the orbital of lower angular momentum. 

(b) For a given value of the principal quantum number, the size of the orbit is inversely proportional to the azimuthal quantum number. 

(c) According to wave mechanics, the ground state angular momentum is equal to $\frac{h}{2π}$.

(d) The plot of $ψ$ vs r for various azimuthal quantum numbers, shows peak shifting towards higher r value.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(a) Angular momentum, $mvr=\frac{nh}{2π}$

$\Rightarrow mvr\propto n$ $\propto$ distance from the nucleus

(b) This statement is incorrect as size of an orbit $\propto$ Azimuthal quantum number (l) ($\because$ n = constant)

(c) This statement is incorrect as at ground state,

n = 1, l = 0

$\Rightarrow$ Orbital angular momentum (wave mechanics)

$=\sqrt{l(l+1)}\frac{h}{2π}=0$ [$\because$ $l=0$]

(d) The plot of $ψ$ vs $r$ for various azimuthal quantum numbers, shows peak shifting towards higher $r$ value.

This statement is typically true. The radial distribution functions of atomic orbitals (which can be related to $|ψ|^{2}$ vs $r$) for higher azimuthal quantum numbers generally have their peaks at larger values of the radial distance $r$ from the nucleus. This is because with higher $l$ values, the electrons are more likely to be found at greater distances due to the higher angular momentum.

text: A solution containing 62 g ethylene glycol in 250 g water is cooled to $-$ $10^{o}C$. If $K_{f}$ for water is 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$ , the amount of water (in g) separated as ice is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ethylene glycol ($\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{6}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$, molar mass $62\text{g mol}^{-1}$): $n=\dfrac{62}{62}=1\text{mol}$. On cooling, only pure water separates as ice; all the glycol stays in the liquid.

At $-10{}^{\circ }\text{C}$, the liquid in equilibrium with ice must have $\Delta T_{f}=0-(-10)=10\text{K}$. If $W$ g of water remains liquid:

$\Delta T_{f}=K_{f}m\Rightarrow 10=1.86\times \dfrac{1}{W/1000}$

$W=\dfrac{1.86\times 1000}{10}=186\text{g}$

Water separated as ice $=250-186=64\text{g}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
The major product of the following reaction is : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$ complexes the lactone carbonyl and cleaves the alkyl C-O bond, giving the primary carbocation $\mathrm{C}^{+}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COO}^{-}$ (as its $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$ complex).

A 1,2-hydride shift converts it into the more stable secondary cation $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{C}^{+}\mathrm{HCH}_{2}\mathrm{COO}^{-}$.

In o-cresol the OH group is the dominant ortho/para director, so the cation attacks para to OH, giving $\mathrm{Ar}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$.

Intramolecular Friedel-Crafts acylation then occurs ortho to the new alkyl group at the position para to $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (the other ortho position is crowded between two substituents), closing a five-membered ring.

The product is the 3-methylindan-1-one in which the $\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})$ carbon is para to OH and the C=O carbon is para to $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
The major product obtained in the following reaction is : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The substrate has two nucleophilic groups, the alcoholic $-\mathrm{OH}$ and the $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ group, and only one equivalent of $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}){}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is used.

Nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen, so its lone pair is more available and $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ is the stronger nucleophile. It attacks a carbonyl carbon of the anhydride first, and with one equivalent of reagent only the amino group is acetylated, giving the amide $-\mathrm{NHCOCH}{}_{3}$ while the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group is left unchanged.

Pyridine only takes up the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}$ formed. At room temperature there is no dehydration of the alcohol (A), ring acylation (B) would need a Lewis acid such as $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$, and O-acetylation (C) is slower than N-acetylation.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
The tests performed on compound X and their inferences are : 

  
    
    Test
    Inference
  
  
    (a)
    2, 4 - DNP test
    Coloured precipitate
  
  
    (b)
    Iodoform test
    Yellow precipitate
  
  
    (c)
    Azo-dye test
    No dye formation
  

Compound 'X' is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A positive 2,4-DNP test shows a carbonyl group (aldehyde or ketone), which rules out compound (C), as it has only an alcohol group.

A positive iodoform test needs a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}{}^{-}$ group; compounds (A) and (D) carry $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}$, not a methyl ketone, so they are ruled out.

No azo dye means there is no primary aromatic amino group that can be diazotised with $\mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}$ and coupled with $β$-naphthol, which also rules out (A).

Compound (B), 2-(dimethylamino)acetophenone, has a methyl ketone, so it gives the 2,4-DNP and iodoform tests, and its tertiary amino group $-\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ cannot form a diazonium salt, so no dye forms.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
The increasing basicity order of the following compounds is : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) In the first compound, because of +I effect of $CH_{3}CH_{2}-$ group electron density increases on N atom.

(B) In the second compound, because of +I effect of two $CH_{3}CH_{2}-$ group electron density is more on N atom than first compound so it is more basic than compound A.

(C) Three $-CH_{3}$ group creates steric hindrance around N atom, for that reason N atom can't donate lone pair easily.

(D) Here lone pair of N atom participates in resonance with benzene ring so N atom can't donate lone pair. That is why it is least basic among this four compounds.

So correct order is D < C < A < B.
